raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

The Responses API accepts `tool_choice={"type": "allowed_tools", ...}`, but the Python server ignored it: calls were not limited to the allowed tools, and non-streaming responses returned them as message text. This change makes the server use the structural-tag support for `allowed_tools` that already exists. It replaces #56368, whose named-`tool_choice` part is now covered by #59723.

## Claims

- When a structural tag applies (the default `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=true`, with a tool parser that supports structural tags), an `allowed_tools` choice limits tool calls to the listed functions. `mode="required"` requires a call; `mode="auto"` also allows a text reply.
- Non-streaming responses return `allowed_tools` calls as `function_call` items, as streaming responses already did.
- `function` entries are resolved like a named `tool_choice` (#59723), so a namespace function can be listed by its local name. Unknown or ambiguous names get a 400, as for a named `tool_choice`, and the not-found message now names the missing tool.
- With `mode="auto"`, a requested `text.format` still applies: the model either calls an allowed function or returns output in that format.
- Entries for built-in tools (for example `web_search` or `mcp`) are ignored for models that are only shown function tools, instead of failing grammar construction.
- The `hf` response-template parser rejects `allowed_tools` with a 400, as it already does for the other tool guarantees it cannot enforce.

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU):

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py \
  tests/tool_use/test_responses_request_validations.py tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py \
  tests/parser/test_abstract_parser.py tests/parser/test_parse.py tests/parser/test_streaming.py \
  tests/parser/test_response_template.py tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py
```

683 passed, 1 xfailed. All 7 new test cases fail with `main`'s source files. Reverting any one of the 7 changed hunks makes at least one of them fail.

Live A/B on CPU: `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` (revision `7ae55760`) with `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --structured-outputs-config.backend xgrammar`, temperature 0. Both runs used the same CPU build of `main` (`0f112d1`); the second added this change. The tools were a plain `get_weather` function and a `crm` namespace containing `lookup`, both `strict`. The prompt was "Look up the customer ACME." Every request was sent both non-streaming and streaming.

| `tool_choice` | `main`, non-streaming | `main`, streaming | This PR (both) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| allowed, required, `lookup` (local name) | message text `<tool_call>{"name": "crm__lookup", ...}` | `crm` / `lookup` call | `crm` / `lookup` call |
| allowed, required, only `get_weather` | message text calling `crm__lookup` | `crm` / `lookup` call (not allowed) | `get_weather` call |
| allowed, auto, only `get_weather` | message text calling `crm__lookup` | `crm` / `lookup` call (not allowed) | `get_weather` call |
| allowed, auto, `lookup`, with `text.format` | formatted JSON text | formatted JSON text | `crm` / `lookup` call |
| allowed, unknown name | 200, unconstrained | 200, unconstrained | 400, `Tool choice 'nonexistent' not found` |
| allowed, `lookup` defined in two namespaces | 200, unconstrained | 200, unconstrained | 400, ambiguous |
| named `lookup` (control) | `crm` / `lookup` call | `crm` / `lookup` call | unchanged |

With this change, an `allowed_tools` list of `lookup` plus `{"type": "web_search"}` (with a `web_search` tool in `tools`) also returned a `crm` / `lookup` call in both modes. With `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=false`, `allowed_tools` is still not enforced, as now documented, but non-streaming responses return the calls as `function_call` items.

Pre-commit passes on the changed files, including mypy for Python 3.10 (commit hook) and 3.12 (manual stage).

Not validated: GPU runs, other tool parsers end to end, and accuracy evals. This change only affects which calls the grammar permits for `allowed_tools` requests.

## Details

Root cause: #45396 added `allowed_tools` handling to the structural-tag registry (`get_structural_tag_tools`, `_dump_tool_choice_for_xgrammar`). However, `DelegatingParser._apply_structural_tag` only builds a tag for `auto`, `required` and named choices, so the server never reached that code. `_extract_tool_calls` also only runs the tool parser for `auto`, so non-streaming responses returned the raw call markup. Streaming already fell through to the auto parser.

Changes:

- `_apply_structural_tag` now builds the tag for `ToolChoiceAllowed`. For structured outputs, `mode="auto"` follows the `auto` path, and the forced variant keeps the allowed subset (`mode="required"`) instead of switching to plain `"required"`.
- `_extract_tool_calls` parses `allowed_tools` calls like `auto`.
- `get_model_structural_tag` drops non-function entries for models outside `_BUILTIN_TOOL_STRUCTURAL_TAG_MODELS`, matching `get_structural_tag_tools`, and builds no tag when no function entry remains. Otherwise xgrammar rejects such entries ("Allowed builtin tools are not found"), and an empty list yields a grammar that does not compile for GLM-4.7 and PLaMo3.
- `ResponsesRequest.check_tool_usage` resolves the `function` entries with `_resolve_named_tool_choice`, so local namespace names reach xgrammar as `namespace__function`.
- `ResponseTemplateParser` lists `allowed_tools` among the guarantees it cannot enforce.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- `allowed_tools` gets a structural tag, and so a per-token grammar cost, even when no tool is `strict`, unlike plain `auto`, because the tag is what limits the calls.
- Unknown or ambiguous `function` entries now fail with a 400 at request validation, including on servers that do not enforce the list. This matches named `tool_choice` validation. Before, these requests failed during grammar construction, or the list was ignored.
- A `namespace` key on an entry is not interpreted, as for a named `tool_choice`. An ambiguous local name must use the full `namespace__function` name.
- Without structural tags, `allowed_tools` is still not enforced. Mapping it onto the JSON-schema path is out of scope. Harmony models build their own tag from all tools and are unchanged by the entry filtering.

Duplicate check: no open PR or issue covers `allowed_tools` in the Python server. I searched PRs and issues for `allowed_tools`, `"allowed tools"` and `ToolChoiceAllowed`. #51535 and #44280 cover the Rust frontend, #45512 covers MCP `allowed_tools` at tool execution time, and #53099 refactors structural-tag capabilities without changing this gate.

I used AI assistance (Claude) to investigate, implement and test this change and to write this description.

@@ -102,6 +102,12 @@ vLLM supports the `tool_choice='required'` option in the chat completion API. Si
 
 When tool_choice='required' is set, the model is guaranteed to generate one or more tool calls based on the specified tool list in the `tools` parameter. The number of tool calls depends on the user's query. The output format strictly follows the schema defined in the `tools` parameter.
 
+## Allowed Tools
+
+In the Responses API, `tool_choice={"type": "allowed_tools", "mode": "auto", "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "..."}]}` keeps every tool in the prompt but limits which functions the model can call. With `mode="required"` the model must call at least one of them; with `mode="auto"` it can also reply with text. Function entries are resolved like a named `tool_choice`, so a namespace function can be listed by its local name or by its full `namespace__function` name.
+
+The limit is enforced with structural tags, so it requires `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=true` (the default) and a tool parser that builds a structural tag for the request. For models that are only shown function tools, entries for built-in tools are ignored. Without a structural tag, tool calls are extracted as with `tool_choice="auto"`; the `hf` parser rejects the request instead, because it cannot enforce the limit.
+
 ## None Function Calling
 
 vLLM supports the `tool_choice='none'` option in the chat completion API. When this option is set, the model will not generate any tool calls and will respond with regular text content only, even if tools are defined in the request.
